deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages). X is a space with a finite stratification by closed strata X_i, indexed by a poset I, with X_i ⊂ X_j iff i ≤ j. The frontier/intersection condition says X_h ∩ X_i = ⋃_{ℓ ≤ h,i} X_ℓ. Notation:
- Ẋ_i = ⋃_{ℓ<i} X_ℓ is the 'bord' (singular part) of X_i.
- X_i^* = X_i \ Ẋ_i is the open stratum.

The stated programme (previous page) is to reconstruct X from the open strata X_i^*, generalising §1. In §1 there were two strata Y ⊂ X, and one used the tube U_{Y,X}.

This page opens §3, 'Stratifications globales : introduction aux tubes'.
- (1) For each pair i ≤ j, V̄_{ij} is a closed tubular (regular) neighbourhood of X_i in X_j.
- (3) For i, j, R_i = ⋃{X_k : X_k ⊉ X_i} is a closed part of X, and R_{ij} = R_i ∩ X_j. This is the union of the strata 'not incident above X_i'.
- (2) The tube's 'bad boundary' is V̇_{ij} = V̄_{ij} ∩ R_i (= V̄_{ij} ∩ R_{ij}, since V̄_{ij} ⊂ X_j).
- (3bis), marginal NB: R_{ij} = ⋃{X_h : h < j, X_h ∩ X_i ≠ X_i}, so R_{ij} ⊂ Ẋ_j.
- (4) R_i ∩ X_i = Ẋ_i.

Proof of (4).
- Suppose X_h ⊉ X_i. Then X_h ∩ X_i = ⋃_{ℓ ≤ h,i} X_ℓ. Each such X_ℓ is properly contained in X_i (otherwise X_i ⊂ X_h). So ℓ < i and X_ℓ ⊂ Ẋ_i, giving R_i ∩ X_i ⊂ Ẋ_i.
- The reverse inclusion is called trivial: for ℓ < i, X_ℓ ⊉ X_i, so X_ℓ ⊂ R_i.

Next page.
- V_{ij} = V̄_{ij} \ R_{ij} is an open tube around X_i^*, with V_{ij} ∩ X_i = X_i^*.
- V*_{ij} = V̄_{ij} \ Ẋ_j = V_{ij} ∩ X_j^* is the deleted tube, lying in the open stratum X_j^*.
- For i = j these degenerate to X_i, Ẋ_i, X_i^*.
- The 'pierres' (building blocks) are the diagrams X_j^* ← V*_{ij} → V_{ij} → X_i^*, the last map being the retraction ('âme') onto the core.

In modern terms, Grothendieck is assembling the data of strata plus homotopy links (deleted tubular neighbourhoods) with their maps to the two strata. The aim is to recover the stratified space, or its stratified homotopy type, by gluing. That is the programme of Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology, 'dévissage' of stratified structures). Today it is realised via Thom–Mather control data, Quinn's homotopy links, and exit-path ∞-categories.
errors: Notation is inconsistent between R*_{i,j}, R_{i*}, R_i and R_{ij}. (2) mixes R_i and R_{ij}; this is harmless because V̄_{ij} ⊂ X_j.
(3bis) holds only for i ≤ j. If X_k ⊉ X_i and j ≤ k, then X_i ⊂ X_j ⊂ X_k, a contradiction, so only strata h < j occur. This uses i ≤ j, which is not stated in (3bis).
The 'trivial' reverse inclusion in (4) tacitly needs X_ℓ ≠ X_i for ℓ < i, i.e. i ↦ X_i injective (nonempty open strata). The proof also uses the frontier condition X_h ∩ X_i = ⋃_{ℓ≤h,i} X_ℓ.
Minor slip: 'X_h ∩ X_i ⊂ Ẋ' should read Ẋ_i.

ideas.what: Closed tubular neighbourhoods V̄_{ij} of each closed stratum X_i in each larger closed stratum X_j, indexed by pairs i ≤ j of the stratification poset.
ideas.modern_name: Control data / system of tubular neighbourhoods
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tubular neighbourhoods and dévissage of stratified tame spaces informally

ideas.what: R_i = union of the closed strata not containing X_i, with R_i ∩ X_i = Ẋ_i. This lets one cut the tube down to an open tube V_{ij} around the open stratum X_i^* alone.
ideas.modern_name: Removal of non-incident strata; open star/tube of a stratum

ideas.what: Building blocks: diagrams X_j^* ← V*_{ij} → V_{ij} → X_i^* (deleted tube and retraction onto core), intended to reconstruct X from its open strata by gluing.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links / holinks; exit-path category data; reconstruction of stratified spaces from strata and links
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (1988), Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches the reconstruction of tame stratified spaces from strata and tubular data

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful set-up of tube notation for a poset-indexed stratification, with an elementary lemma (R_i ∩ X_i = Ẋ_i). The reconstruction-from-tubes programme is known from the Esquisse and is realised in later work (Quinn, Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka); nothing on this page goes beyond that.

In (3) the condition under the union is 'k ∈ I tels que X_k ⊅ X_i' (a crossed-out word precedes X_k).
In (4) the first term is R*_{i,j} ∩ X_i (starred, overwritten), not 'R_{i*}'.
The proof's conclusion reads 'X_h ∩ X_i ⊂ Ẋ' with the subscript i missing in the manuscript.
The marginal NB reads 'NB On a aussi R_{ij} = ⋃_{h<j, tel que X_h ∩ X_i ≠ X_i} X_h ⊂ Ẋ_j' (3bis). The transcription separated the parts.
